findings.message: 114 says the mock 'escapes the text it puts into HTML', but this change escapes only the nav sheet and srTable. `window.amaxAddDeal` still puts chat-extracted fields (d.client, d.name, d.value, d.win, d.close) into `c.innerHTML` raw. `extract()` takes d.name and d.close from whatever the user types (`[^,.]{4,60}` and the date regex). This is the same 'DOM text reinterpreted as HTML' alert that 114 fixes elsewhere. Fix: pass every interpolated field through `window.amaxEsc`, and check the other innerHTML sinks that take data (4187 s.dataset.title, 4294/4387 p[0], 4649 p[0]/d.note, 4718 o.title/o.hint) the same way.
findings.scenario: Open chat, pick 'Fill with amax' (opportunity), type 'Contoso is interested in worth 50k led by Liam', then press 'Add it'. The deal card renders the and its onerror runs.

findings.message: The fix for log injection (a B8 class) cleans three inputs: scope, the error's code and the error's name. The variant table covers only two of them: a newline in the scope and in the code. Nothing checks `oneWord(name)`, and the table is below the minimum of the named case plus two others. Fix: add a row for an Error whose `name` holds '\nFAKE amax admin: ok', and one for a non-Error thrown value.
findings.scenario: Change `oneWord(name)` back to `name` in log.ts. Every test still passes, but `logError('chat', Object.assign(new Error('x'), { name: 'E\nFAKE amax admin: ok' }))` writes a forged second log line.

findings.message: The new top-level `esc` (escapes & < > " ') is a second copy of the chat's own `esc` at line 4477, which escapes only & < >. The two disagree on quotes. Today the chat copy is used only in element text, so nothing renders wrong yet. Fix: have the chat use `window.amaxEsc` and delete its local `esc`.
Changing `() =>` to `(_h) =>` in `cover` and `later` does nothing: the parameter is never used, and `Step` already allows a zero-argument function. Revert both lines.
